Area.evidence_source: Male suicide continues to be a significant health issue attracting diverse research attention ranging from epidemiological studies (Statistics Canada, 2017) to men's lived experiences of suicidality (Kealy, Joyce, Abbass, Oliffe, & Ogrodniczuk, 2016). This research is vitally important; yet the gendered experiences of men bereaved by male suicide are poorly understood. This knowledge gap is noteworthy, especially in light of the high male suicide rates in Western countries (Statistics Canada, 2017), and estimates that 45 to 80 people are directly affected by each suicide (Berman, 2011). The current study and article describes connections between masculinities and men's suicide bereavement contributing important insights to guide community and programmatic services.
